title: Beta Israel tradition of bringing the Ark via Elephantine
summary: Graham Hancock tells of Beta Israel tradition of bringing the Ark via Elephantine, about c. 650-400 BC at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

as_told.title: Falasha (Beta Israel) tradition of the Ark's journey to Ethiopia
as_told.place_text: Israel; island in the Nile; Lake Tana, Ethiopia

plain: A writer on ancient mysteries, Graham Hancock, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about the Beta Israel, also called Falashas, a Jewish community of Ethiopia. Hancock says their tradition holds that their ancestors fled Israel carrying the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest of the Bible, and brought it to Elephantine, an island in the Nile in Egypt. In his later telling he adds that they kept it there for several hundred years before taking it on to Ethiopia, and he connects this to the Kebra Nagast, an old Ethiopian holy book. If true, it would mean the Ark ended up in Ethiopia.
